questions.stem: In this diagram of the vagus and phrenic nerves in the thorax, the left recurrent laryngeal nerve is shown hooking around a specific structure before ascending back to the larynx. questions.stem: This dissection shows the papillary muscles connected to the AV valve leaflets by thin cords (chordae tendineae). What is the function of this papillary muscle–chordae apparatus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Supplies oxygenated blood to the myocardium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Anchors the great vessels to the pericardium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Opens the semilunar valves during ejection

questions.stem: The vessel labeled here with its anatomical name, the 'anterior interventricular artery,' is more commonly known by which clinical name?

explanation.summary: The anterior interventricular artery, a branch of the left main coronary artery running in the anterior interventricular groove, is clinically termed the left anterior descending (LAD). It supplies the anterior LV wall, anterior two-thirds of the septum, and apex.

questions.stem: In this coronary angiogram, the right coronary artery is seen continuing to give off the posterior descending artery. What does this finding indicate about the coronary circulation?

explanation.summary: Coronary dominance is defined by the origin of the posterior descending artery (PDA). When the PDA arises from the RCA, as here, the patient has a right-dominant circulation, the most common pattern (~85%).
explanation.whyCorrect: Coronary dominance is defined by the origin of the posterior descending artery (PDA). When the PDA arises from the RCA, as here, the patient has a right-dominant circulation, the most common pattern (~85%).

explanation.summary: The insets illustrate an atherosclerotic plaque (lipid core with fibrous cap) encroaching on the coronary lumen. Progressive stenosis limits myocardial perfusion and, with plaque rupture and thrombosis, precipitates acute coronary syndromes.

questions.stem: This diagram of the heart wall and its coverings shows a fluid-filled space between two serous membranes. What is the primary physiologic function of this space and its fluid?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It conducts the electrical impulse from SA to AV node

choices.label: C
choices.text: It stores oxygenated blood for coronary perfusion

choices.label: D
choices.text: It anchors the chordae tendineae to the papillary muscles

choices.label: E
choices.text: It secretes hormones that regulate heart rate

questions.stem: This muscle tissue is composed of branching cells joined end to end, each with a single central nucleus and abundant pink cytoplasm, supported by delicate connective tissue and capillaries. What tissue is this?

explanation.summary: Branching fibers with single central nuclei and interposed capillaries are diagnostic of cardiac muscle, distinguishing it from multinucleated peripheral-nucleus skeletal muscle and spindle-shaped smooth muscle.
explanation.whyCorrect: Branching fibers with single central nuclei and interposed capillaries are diagnostic of cardiac muscle, distinguishing it from multinucleated peripheral-nucleus skeletal muscle and spindle-shaped smooth muscle.

questions.stem: The magnified inset (red arrow) highlights a darker transverse band crossing a cardiac muscle fiber at the junction between two cells. What structure is indicated, and what is its function?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A motor end plate transmitting nerve impulses to the fiber

choices.label: B
choices.text: A band of collagen anchoring the cell to the endomysium

choices.label: C
choices.text: A T-tubule invagination triggering calcium release

choices.label: D

choices.label: E

explanation.summary: Intercalated discs are specialized step-like junctions between cardiomyocytes containing desmosomes/fasciae adherentes (mechanical linkage) and gap junctions (electrical continuity), enabling the myocardium to contract as a functional syncytium.

questions.stem: On this combined pressure and LV volume tracing, ventricular volume reaches its minimum (ESV) immediately after which event?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Atrial contraction adding the final filling volume

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aortic valve closure at the end of ejection

questions.stem: In the normal S2 shown at the top, why does the A2-P2 split widen during inspiration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The mitral valve closes earlier during inspiration

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased venous return delays pulmonic valve closure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Systemic vascular resistance falls during inspiration

explanation.summary: Inspiration lowers intrathoracic pressure, augmenting venous return to the right heart. The larger right ventricular volume prolongs right ventricular ejection, delaying pulmonic (P2) closure and thereby widening the physiologic splitting of S2.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inspiration lowers intrathoracic pressure, augmenting venous return to the right heart. The larger right ventricular volume prolongs right ventricular ejection, delaying pulmonic (P2) closure and thereby widening the physiologic splitting of S2.
